content.raw:
Dr Jeremy Sun, also listed professionally as Sun Mingfa Jeremy and on this site as Dr Jeremy Sun Mingfa, is the same Singapore plastic surgeon. His CGH doctor listing provides an institutional profile. Lymphedema Asia focuses on lymphoedema and lymphatic surgery education; his personal professional website covers his broader plastic, reconstructive and aesthetic practice.

Dr Jeremy Sun Mingfa is a Singapore plastic and reconstructive surgeon with a focused clinical interest in lymphedema, lymphatic reconstruction, supermicrosurgery and specialist assessment for patients with persistent limb swelling. This page explains his training background, clinical approach and how patients can think about options such as compression, ICG lymphography, lymphovenous bypass / LVA, vascularized lymph node transfer and longer-term lymphedema care.

Private consultation enquiries: Contact Astrid Plastic Surgery or enquire on WhatsApp at +65 8764 9219. These routes are for non-urgent appointment enquiries.

Who is a lymphedema specialist or surgeon in Singapore?

A lymphedema specialist or lymphedema surgeon should be able to assess the cause and stage of swelling, review conservative care, arrange lymphatic imaging when appropriate and explain whether surgery is suitable. In Singapore, patients may need input from therapists, vascular or rehabilitation teams, oncologic teams and plastic surgeons with lymphatic surgery training, depending on the problem.

Dr Jeremy Sun Mingfa is a Senior Consultant plastic and reconstructive surgeon in Singapore with a focused clinical interest in lymphedema, LVA / lymphovenous bypass surgery and lymphatic reconstruction. His assessment approach considers ICG lymphography, ultrasound localisation, infection history, compression response, stage of disease and realistic goals before discussing options such as continued conservative care, LVA, vascularized lymph node transfer, liposuction or debulking where relevant.

This information is educational and does not replace an individual medical consultation. Suitability, risks, recovery and outcomes vary between patients.

Why patients seek a lymphedema specialist

Lymphedema is not simply ordinary swelling. It may follow cancer surgery, lymph node removal, radiotherapy, trauma, infection or primary lymphatic-development issues. Some patients present with arm or leg swelling, recurrent cellulitis, heaviness, skin thickening, difficulty using compression garments, or uncertainty about whether surgery is appropriate.

A specialist assessment should consider the cause of swelling, the stage of disease, tissue characteristics, infection history, prior treatment and whether imaging shows lymphatic channels that may be suitable for procedures such as LVA.

Dedicated lymphatic surgery training in Japan

Dr Sun undertook dedicated HMDP fellowship training in comprehensive multidisciplinary lymphoedema management and lymphatic surgery in Japan, with focused exposure to lymphedema assessment, ICG lymphography, ultrasound localisation and supermicrosurgical lymphatic reconstruction. This training reinforced an approach based on careful patient selection rather than offering one procedure to every patient.

Assessment before deciding on surgery

Before discussing surgery, a consultation usually clarifies whether swelling is fluid-dominant, fibrotic, fatty, mixed, venous-related, cancer-treatment-related, primary, or due to another cause. This distinction matters because the best plan may involve compression optimisation, therapy, infection prevention, LVA, lymph node transfer, reductive surgery, or a staged combination. When swelling is painful, symmetrical or associated with disproportionate limb fat, patients may also need assessment for lipedema versus lymphedema rather than assuming every swollen limb is the same condition.

How Dr Sun approaches LVA and lymphedema surgery

LVA surgery is a supermicrosurgical procedure that connects suitable lymphatic channels to nearby small veins to create additional drainage pathways. Suitability depends on clinical assessment and imaging. Not every patient with lymphedema is a candidate, and surgery does not usually replace long-term compression or skin care for all patients.

Dr Sun’s lymphedema surgery approach emphasises imaging-guided planning, pressure and flow considerations, compression strategy, realistic counselling and follow-up. For some patients, LVA may be considered; for others, lymph node transfer, reductive procedures, conservative care or combined strategies may be more appropriate.

Questions patients can ask

  • What is the likely cause and stage of my lymphedema?
  • Do I need ICG lymphography, ultrasound mapping or other imaging?
  • Are there functional lymphatic channels suitable for LVA?
  • Would lymph node transfer, reductive surgery or conservative care be more appropriate?
  • How does my cellulitis or infection history affect the plan?
  • What role should compression therapy and long-term follow-up play?

Academic and educational work

Dr Sun is involved in clinical education and academic work related to plastic surgery, reconstructive microsurgery and lymphatic surgery. Educational pages on LymphedAsia are intended to help patients understand options in a balanced way before discussing individual treatment suitability.

Training context: Learn why dedicated lymphedema surgery training and HMDP fellowship selection differ from general microsurgery training or short observerships.

About Lymphedema Asia and Dr Jeremy Sun

What is Lymphedema Asia?

Lymphedema Asia is a Singapore-based educational resource for patients, caregivers and healthcare professionals seeking information on lymphedema, lymphatic surgery, lymphovenous bypass (LVA/LVB), compression therapy and multidisciplinary lymphedema care.

Who is Dr Jeremy Sun?

Dr Jeremy Sun Mingfa is a Senior Consultant Plastic and Reconstructive Surgeon in Singapore with dedicated overseas training in lymphedema surgery and supermicrosurgical lymphatic reconstruction.

Is Lymphedema Asia a clinic?

Lymphedema Asia is primarily an educational resource. Its information supports understanding of lymphedema and treatment options, but it does not replace individual medical consultation. Consultation enquiries should be directed through the appropriate clinic pathway.

Does Lymphedema Asia provide online medical advice?

No. Lymphedema Asia provides educational information only and does not provide personalised online diagnosis or treatment advice. Patients should seek assessment by an appropriate healthcare professional.
